newsitem.title: USA: Aluminum, Brick & Glass Workers vote to merge.
newsitem.headline: Aluminum, Brick & Glass Workers vote to merge.

text.p: The United Steelworkers of America said Tuesday delegates representing the 40,000 Aluminum, Brick & Glass Workers International Union members in the United States and Canada voted Monday night to merge with the Steelworkers.
The action came at a special ABG Merger Convention that convened Monday morning. After a day of debate, more than 400 delegates representing 230 ABG local unions cast their votes by secret ballot.
The vote count, including proxy votes, was 374 to 86, or 81 percent in favor of the merger.
That's well over the two-thirds vote needed for ratification, the Steelworkers said.
The ABG and the USWA have worked together for many years, and "our two unions fit together naturally," USWA President George Becker said.
The merger raises the USWA's membership to about 740,000.
During the debate on the merger, many delegates emphasized the need for greater strength to deal with growing attacks on unions by companies and many governments.
Delegates noted how the USWA had taken up the fight against Bridgestone Corp's Bridgestone/Firestone by the United Rubber Workers, which merged with the USWA in July 1995.
The delegates also noted that by merging with the USWA they will become part of the future unification of the Steelworkers with the Auto Workers and Machinists unions, scheduled for the year 2000.
A proposed merger agreement had been approved by the Executive Committees of the ABG and USWA last August and submitted to the ABG local unions for their review prior to the special Convention.

Under terms of the agreement, the merger will become effective January 20, 1997. Following the merger, all ABG local unions will constitute the Aluminum, Brick and Glass Division of the USWA, with headquarters in St. Louis, Mo., where the ABG is now based. The division will have its own elected officers and a seat on the USWA Executive Board.
